rules: Front ends are not consensus-critical and may be upgraded independently.
420 Registry is the canonical discovery backbone.

420 Wallet Web is the Genesis management client for Wallet Core; Wallet Core reuses 420 Smart Accounts and Capability Registry as the authoritative ownership, recovery, session, capability, revocation and execution layer and creates no parallel wallet authority.

420 Wallet must expose verified Registry/signed-manifest navigation to core ecosystem services including 420 Search, 420 AppStore, 420 AI and 420 Token plus a Developer Hub with user guides, developer guides, protocol specifications, white papers, SDK/API documentation, network/RPC configuration, contract references, source repositories and security documentation.

420 Wallet implementation does not require a final production domain; production URLs remain configuration-driven and WebAuthn/passkey relying-party binding is finalized only after the canonical production domain is selected.
420 Search is a replaceable discovery projection and never becomes authority for indexed records, ranking, ownership, identity, rights, listings, payments or protocol state.

420 Analytics is a replaceable derived-data projection; metrics, KPIs, charts, cohorts, rankings and forecasts never override canonical chain, accounting, identity, rights, governance or settlement state.

420 AppStore is a replaceable catalogue and curation layer; listing, delisting, featuring, ranking, reviews and sponsorship never create or revoke canonical Registry legitimacy or bypass Wallet authorization.

420 Verify is a replaceable reproducible-build verifier; a verified source match never means audited, safe, official, immutable or endorsed, and proxy implementations must be verified independently after upgrades.

420 Notifications is a replaceable opt-in delivery layer; alerts never become authority for underlying events, private delivery/watch data stays private by default, and notification actions cannot bypass Wallet or origin-application authorization.

420 Gaming Protocol is an optional-wallet interoperability layer: games may support guest and conventional accounts without chain interaction, while canonical wallet-linked profiles, entitlements, migration commitments and cross-game attestations reuse Smart Accounts and Capability Registry rather than creating parallel wallet authority.
420 Gaming Protocol does not make routine game saves or progression canonical chain state and wallet connection must not itself grant pay-to-win statistical advantages.
420 Arbitration records dispute process and final rulings but cannot directly execute custody, token transfer, slashing, bridge reversal, rights mutation or governance actions.
420 Token accepts only frozen qualified template IDs, charges exactly 42 native 420 per successful deployment, records provenance, and retains no post-deployment token custody or mint authority.
420 Names never replaces canonical protocol/service identity.
420 Identity is optional and pseudonymous.
420 Stake does not include stake-weighted delegation at genesis.
420 Attention cannot access wallet keys, auto-sign, execute arbitrary wallet code, or transact on behalf of users.

420Arcade ordinary core gameplay remains wallet-free and accessible to guests without registration or blockchain connectivity; optional Gaming Protocol integrations cannot create pay-to-win advantages or separate wallet or contract authority.
420 Faucet never participates in mainnet genesis economics.

Genesis Application Decision #2 authorizes catalog inclusion only. Newly listed application entry points remain disabled until per-application implementation, security, operational and external acceptance; no listed client gains protocol, signing, payment, moderation, or governance authority solely from inclusion.

DOOBr, LIFTd and 420Bet regulated/economic execution remain disabled until applicable jurisdictional, independent risk, legal and production-release approvals. 420Freelance requires independent product implementation qualification despite catalog inclusion.
